fanoutqa_037319.t: 1964 Alaska earthquake :: Death toll, damage, and casualties :: Canada :: chunk_0006
fanoutqa_037319.x:
1964 Alaska earthquake :: Death toll, damage, and casualties :: Canada :: chunk_0006
A 4.5 ft (1.4 m) wave reached [Prince Rupert, British Columbia](/wiki/Prince_Rupert,_British_Columbia "Prince Rupert, British Columbia"), just south of the [Alaska Panhandle](/wiki/Alaska_Panhandle "Alaska Panhandle"), about three hours after the earthquake. The tsunami then reached [Tofino](/wiki/Tofino,_British_Columbia "Tofino, British Columbia"), on the exposed west coast of [Vancouver Island](/wiki/Vancouver_Island "Vancouver Island"), and traveled up a [fjord](/wiki/Alberni_Inlet "Alberni Inlet") to hit [Port Alberni](/wiki/Port_Alberni,_British_Columbia "Port Alberni, British Columbia") twice, washing away 55 homes and damaging 375 others. The towns of [Hot Springs Cove](/wiki/Hot_Springs_Cove,_British_Columbia "Hot Springs Cove, British Columbia"), [Zeballos](/wiki/Zeballos,_British_Columbia "Zeballos, British Columbia"), and [Amai](/w/index.php?title=Amai,_British_Columbia&action=edit&redlink=1 "Amai, British Columbia (page does not exist)") also saw damage.[[20]](#cite_note-21) The damage in British Columbia was estimated at CA$10 million ($100 million in 2025 Canadian dollars or $96 million in 2025 US dollars).[[21]](#cite_note-inflation-CA-22)[[22]](#cite_note-inflation-US-23)

fanoutqa_000711.t: Avatar: The Way of Water :: Themes and analysis :: chunk_0021
fanoutqa_000711.x:
Avatar: The Way of Water :: Themes and analysis :: chunk_0021
Family is the central concept featured in *Avatar: The Way of Water*.[[98]](#cite_note-GMAIntegratedNewsInterview-116)[[244]](#cite_note-265)[[245]](#cite_note-266) *[RogerEbert.com](/wiki/RogerEbert.com "RogerEbert.com")* critic Brian Tallerico notes that some of the themes in the film echo themes from earlier films directed by Cameron, including *[Titanic](/wiki/Titanic_(1997_film) "Titanic (1997 film)")* (1997), *[Aliens](/wiki/Aliens_(film) "Aliens (film)")* (1986), *[The Abyss](/wiki/The_Abyss "The Abyss")* (1989), *[The Terminator](/wiki/The_Terminator "The Terminator")* (1984) and *[Terminator 2: Judgment Day](/wiki/Terminator_2:_Judgment_Day "Terminator 2: Judgment Day")* (1991). For example, the film asks whether you should run and hide from a powerful enemy or fight their evil, similar to the *[Terminator](/wiki/Terminator_(franchise) "Terminator (franchise)")* films. The film also invokes themes of [environmentalism](/wiki/Environmentalism "Environmentalism") and [settler colonialism](/wiki/Settler_colonialism "Settler colonialism").[[246]](#cite_note-ebert-267) Comparing the themes of the sequels to the original, Cameron said "It will be a natural extension of all the themes, and the characters, and the spiritual undercurrents. Basically, if you loved the first movie, you're gonna love these movies, and if you hated it, you're probably gonna hate these. If you loved it at the time, and you said later you hated it, you're probably gonna love these".[[75]](#cite_note-Vanity_Fair_Legacy-86)

Amy Gutmann :: Career :: University of Pennsylvania :: Tenure as president :: chunk_0006
On May 8, 2012, Penn announced that Gutmann's contract had been renewed through 2019.[[53]](#cite_note-53) In announcing the extension, David L. Cohen, chair of Penn's Board of Trustees, stated that Penn's "Trustees feel very strongly that Amy Gutmann is simply the best university president in the country. Under her superb leadership, Penn is a stronger and more vibrant institution than at any time in its storied history."[[54]](#cite_note-54) In November 2016 Cohen, still Board Chairman, announced that Gutmann's contract would be extended until 2022, making her the longest-serving president ever at Penn.[[55]](#cite_note-55)

In 2017, Gutmann's total compensation was $2.9 million, making her the highest paid private college president in Pennsylvania and fourth highest in the United States.[[56]](#cite_note-56)

In 2021, according IRS Form 990 filed by the trustees of the University of Pennsylvania, Gutmann's W-2 reportable compensation was $22,821,735, “the vast majority of it — more than $20 million — was accrued over Gutmann’s nearly two-decade-long tenure as the Ivy League university’s leader and paid out as agreed when it vested, just months before she departed,” according to Sue Snyder of the Philadelphia Inquirer.[[57]](#cite_note-57) Gutmann was also the recipient of a $3.7 million dollar loan from the University of Pennsylvania that remained 100% outstanding as of the end of 2021.[[58]](#cite_note-58)

As an adolescent, Diamond originally intended to study molecular biology. Diamond matriculated at [Brown University](/wiki/Brown_University "Brown University"), where he decided to study economics instead, after taking a course on [Milton Friedman](/wiki/Milton_Friedman "Milton Friedman") and [Anna Schwartz](/wiki/Anna_J._Schwartz "Anna J. Schwartz")'s *[A Monetary History of the United States](/wiki/A_Monetary_History_of_the_United_States "A Monetary History of the United States")*.[[7]](#cite_note-:4-7)[[8]](#cite_note-:5-8) He graduated [Phi Beta Kappa](/wiki/Phi_Beta_Kappa "Phi Beta Kappa") from Brown with a Bachelor of Arts degree in economics in 1975.[[9]](#cite_note-www.chicagobooth.edu-9) The following year, and in 1977 Diamond earned master's degrees, and ultimately a PhD in economics in 1980 from [Yale University](/wiki/Yale_University "Yale University").[[9]](#cite_note-www.chicagobooth.edu-9) At Yale, both Diamond and future Nobel co-recipient Philip H. Dybvig were advised by [Stephen A. Ross](/wiki/Stephen_Ross_(economist) "Stephen Ross (economist)"). fanoutqa_029383.t: Philadelphia 76ers :: History :: 1964–1968: Wilt Chamberlain era :: 1966–1967: First title in Philadelphia :: chunk_0007
fanoutqa_029383.x:
Philadelphia 76ers :: History :: 1964–1968: Wilt Chamberlain era :: 1966–1967: First title in Philadelphia :: chunk_0007
Led by head coach [Alex Hannum](/wiki/Alex_Hannum "Alex Hannum"), the 76ers had a dream season: starting 46–4[[17]](#cite_note-nba10-19) and finishing 68–13, the best record in league history at the time.[[18]](#cite_note-best-20) Chamberlain, [Billy Cunningham](/wiki/Billy_Cunningham "Billy Cunningham"), and Greer, along with all-stars [Chet Walker](/wiki/Chet_Walker "Chet Walker"), [Lucious Jackson](/wiki/Lucious_Jackson "Lucious Jackson"), and [Wali Jones](/wiki/Wali_Jones "Wali Jones") led the team to the semifinals, where the 76ers beat the Celtics in five games, ending Boston's eight-year reign as NBA champions. [The Finals](/wiki/1967_NBA_Finals "1967 NBA Finals") were almost anticlimactic; the Sixers beat the Warriors in six games to earn their second NBA championship. During the [NBA's 35th anniversary celebration](/wiki/NBA_35th_Anniversary_Team "NBA 35th Anniversary Team") in 1980, the [1966–67 76ers](/wiki/1966%E2%80%9367_Philadelphia_76ers_season "1966–67 Philadelphia 76ers season") would be voted the best team in league history.

In the [1967–68 season](/wiki/1967%E2%80%9368_NBA_season "1967–68 NBA season"), with a new home court at [The Spectrum](/wiki/Spectrum_(arena) "Spectrum (arena)"), the 76ers returned to the playoffs. In a rematch of the previous year's semifinals, the 76ers held a 3–1 series lead before the Celtics rallied to win in seven games.

Yellowstone ranks among the most popular national parks in the United States. Since the mid-1960s, at least 2 million tourists have visited the park almost every year.[[165]](#cite_note-Visitation-168) Average annual visitation increased to 3.5 million during the ten years from 2007 to 2016, with a record of 4,257,177 recreational visitors in 2016.[[166]](#cite_note-visits-169) This number was surpassed in 2023 with 4.5 million people visiting the park.[[167]](#cite_note-170) July is the busiest month.[[168]](#cite_note-171) At peak summer levels, 3,700 employees work for Yellowstone National Park concessionaires. Concessionaires manage nine hotels and lodges, with a total of 2,238 hotel rooms and cabins available. They also oversee gas stations, stores, and most of the campgrounds. Another 800 employees work either permanently or seasonally for the National Park Service.[[11]](#cite_note-facts-11)[[169]](#cite_note-172)

In late 2009, the "Twitter Lists" feature was added, making it possible for users to follow a curated list of accounts all at once, rather than following individual users.[[98]](#cite_note-lists1-101)[[144]](#cite_note-147) Currently, lists can be set to either public or private. Public lists may be recommended to users via the general Lists interface and appear in search results.[[145]](#cite_note-148) If a user follows a public list, it will appear in the "View Lists" section of their profile, so that other users may quickly find it and follow it as well.[[146]](#cite_note-149) Private lists can only be followed if the creator shares a specific link to their list. Lists add a separate tab to the Twitter interface with the title of the list, such as "News" or "Economics".

In October 2015, Twitter introduced "Moments"—a feature that allows users to curate tweets from other users into a larger collection. Twitter initially intended the feature to be used by its in-house editorial team and other partners; they populated a dedicated tab in Twitter's apps, chronicling news headlines, sporting events, and other content.[[147]](#cite_note-150)[[148]](#cite_note-151) In September 2016, creation of moments became available to all Twitter users.[[149]](#cite_note-152)

If I walk, will you walk with me?".[[27]](#cite_note-30) At the funeral, William and Harry walked alongside their father, grandfather, and maternal uncle, [Charles Spencer, 9th Earl Spencer](/wiki/Charles_Spencer,_9th_Earl_Spencer "Charles Spencer, 9th Earl Spencer"), behind the funeral cortège from Kensington Palace to [Westminster Abbey](/wiki/Westminster_Abbey "Westminster Abbey").[[28]](#cite_note-31)

After his mother's death, William stated that he had been "in a state of shock for many years".[[29]](#cite_note-gq-32) He and Harry inherited the majority of the £12.9 million left by their mother on their respective 30th birthdays, a figure that had grown to £10 million each by 2014.[[30]](#cite_note-BBCJan2020-33)[[31]](#cite_note-Teleg14-34) In 2014, the brothers inherited [their mother's wedding dress](/wiki/Wedding_dress_of_Lady_Diana_Spencer "Wedding dress of Lady Diana Spencer"), along with many of her personal possessions, including dresses, diamond tiaras, jewels, letters, and paintings. In 2008, cancer was responsible for 25% of all US deaths, with 30% of these from lung cancer. In 2008, the most commonly occurring cancer in men was [prostate cancer](/wiki/Prostate_cancer "Prostate cancer"), at about 25% of new cases. In 2008, amongst women, [breast cancer](/wiki/Breast_cancer "Breast cancer") was the most commonly occurring cancer, with about 25% of cancer diagnoses. Cancer can occur in children and adolescents, but it is uncommon, with about 150 cases per million in the U.S., with [leukemia](/wiki/Leukemia "Leukemia") being the most common.[[22]](#cite_note-Jemal-22) In the first year of life, the [incidence](/wiki/Incidence_(epidemiology) "Incidence (epidemiology)") is about 230 cases per million in the U.S., with the most common being [neuroblastoma](/wiki/Neuroblastoma "Neuroblastoma").[[28]](#cite_note-28) From 2004 to 2008, the US overall age-adjusted [incidence](/wiki/Incidence_(epidemiology) "Incidence (epidemiology)") of cancer was approximately 460 per 100,000 men and women per year.[[29]](#cite_note-29)

In 2008, cancer was responsible for about 25% of all US deaths. The statistics below are estimates for the U.S. in 2008, and may vary substantially in other countries. They exclude basal and squamous cell skin cancers, and [carcinoma in situ](/wiki/Carcinoma_in_situ "Carcinoma in situ") in locations other than the urinary bladder.[[22]](#cite_note-Jemal-22) As seen, breast/prostate cancer, lung cancer and colorectal cancer are responsible for approximately half of cancer incidence. The same applies for cancer mortality, but with lung cancer replacing breast/prostate cancer as the main cause.

In 2016, an estimated 1,685,210 new cases of cancer will be diagnosed in the United States and 595,690 people will die from the disease.[[30]](#cite_note-30)
